sentences.text: To address the unclear relationship between memory process variables and executive functioning, researchers examined 127 adults with brain tumors, a group averaging 56.7 years of age with 63.8% female participants.

During both the learning and delayed recall phases of the memory test, these participants demonstrated lower levels of semantic clustering, a strategy involving grouping related words, compared to healthy controls.
Executive functioning scores were positively associated with the use of semantic clustering, but no such association was found with the number of intrusions or repetitions.
The measured memory process variables did not vary based on the location of the tumor within the brain.
